meta.title: Operation of Gas Chromatograph (GC) in Pharmaceutical Analysis Laboratory

sections.purpose: To separate, identify, and quantify volatile components of pharmaceutical preparations including residual solvents, essential oils, and volatile impurities as per pharmacopeial methods (IP, BP, USP).
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmaceutical Analysis laboratory for residual solvent testing (ICH Q3C), essential oil profiling, purity determination of volatile pharmaceutical compounds, and verification of solvent identity.
procedure: Switch on the GC system (injector, column oven, detector) and allow the system to warm up with carrier gas flowing for a minimum of 30 minutes.
Set carrier gas (helium or nitrogen) flow rate as per the method: typically 1–2 mL/min for capillary columns.
Set injector temperature (typically 200–250°C for most pharmaceutical applications); set detector temperature 20–30°C above the highest column temperature.
Set the oven temperature program per the validated method (e.g., isothermal at 40°C, or programmed ramp for multi-component separations).
Allow the system to reach the set temperatures and stabilize (typically 20–30 minutes).
Establish a stable baseline on the chromatogram display — a drifting baseline indicates system instability or column bleed.
Prepare the sample solution as per the validated method: dissolve in the specified solvent (e.g., DMF, water, headspace vial for headspace GC).
Inject the reference standard solution first: use a clean 10 µL microsyringe; inject 1–2 µL through the septum with a rapid plunger push.
Verify the standard chromatogram: retention time and peak area should match previous validated runs.
Inject the sample solution using the same volume and technique.
Record the chromatogram; note retention times and peak areas for all peaks.
Calculate results: for residual solvents — compare sample peak area against standard; apply ICH Q3C limits.
Clean the microsyringe with 5 injections of the injection solvent between standard and sample.
After analysis, set the oven to standby temperature (30°C); allow to cool before shutting down; turn off carrier gas last.
Record all parameters, sample IDs, run numbers, and results in the analytical register.
precautions: Always establish stable baseline before injecting samples — an unstable baseline causes integration errors.
Handle microsyringes with extreme care — the needle is very fine and bends easily; never discard in regular trash.
Replace the septum regularly — a cored or damaged septum causes air leaks and ghost peaks.
Purge the column with carrier gas before and after each batch to remove contaminating residues.
Do not allow the column temperature to exceed the maximum rated temperature — column stationary phase bleeds at high temperatures.
Verify detector sensitivity daily using a check standard.
For flammable carrier gases (hydrogen), ensure proper gas leak testing before lighting the detector.
